note: A review pass over 0.071: fifteen defects found by reading the code that shipped it. The simulation engine again produces identical numbers — its 309 golden reference lines are bit-for-bit what 0.071 produced — but four things here DO change results on particular files, and each is called out in the changelog: Auto aero could miss a supersonic flight on a staged design whose booster waits on a pad timer (the short probe never counted the ignition delays themselves), Auto aero now re-checks the finished flight and re-flies if the real peak Mach crossed 0.9, and two RASAero .CDX1 import fixes for files whose simulations leave the last booster out. Also: a time step you chose yourself now survives an upgrade instead of being quietly reset by every release, saving as .CDX1 keeps stage separation delays, batch simulate warns what a fine time step costs before it starts, combination batches got back the short probe that never took effect, the seconds-per-flight estimate measures one flight again, and every notice that promised something the app cannot do now says what is true.
